meta.description: Verified: Napoleon Hill wrote it in The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons (1928), Lesson Eleven. It is not the line from Think and Grow Rich.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Strong, deeply rooted desire is the starting point of all achievement'?
meta.ogDescription: Verified in Napoleon Hill's 1928 Law of Success course, Lesson Eleven, under the sub-heading DESIRE — not in Think and Grow Rich.

answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: 1883–1970 · American self-help author, creator of the 1928 Law of Success course
answer.sourceLine: The sentence is genuine and appears word for word in Hill’s The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons (Ralston University Press, 1928), in Lesson Eleven, “Accurate Thought,” under the sub-heading DESIRE. It is not from Think and Grow Rich, where Hill later put the same idea in different words.

source.heading: Where the line actually appears

docMeta.dd: The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons
Lesson Eleven, “Accurate Thought” — under the sub-heading DESIRE

source.excerpt:
DESIRE

Strong, deeply rooted desire is the starting point of all achievement. Just as the electron is the last unit of matter discernible to the scientist, DESIRE is the seed of all achievement; the starting place, back of which there is nothing, or at least there is nothing of which we have any knowledge.

A definite chief aim, which is only another name for DESIRE, would be meaningless unless based upon a deeply seated, strong desire for the object of the chief aim. Many people “wish” for many things, but a wish is not the equivalent of a strong DESIRE, and therefore wishes are of little or no value unless they are crystallized into the more definite form of DESIRE.
trail: Wikiquote’s sourced list for Hill files this sentence under The Law of Success (1928) — not under his later books — giving the exact wording in circulation today (Wikiquote: Napoleon Hill ↗).

We checked that against the text itself. An Internet Archive scan of the 1928 Ralston University Press printing carries the sentence verbatim in Lesson Eleven, “Accurate Thought,” immediately under the sub-heading DESIRE (1928 full text ↗).

A full text of Think and Grow Rich does not contain this sentence at all. Its closest lines are the chapter heading “Desire: The Starting Point of All Achievement” and, twice in the body, “The starting point of all achievement is DESIRE” (Think and Grow Rich full text ↗).
Quote Investigator has never taken this line up — a site search for the phrase returns no entry about it, so there is no competing origin claim on record (Quote Investigator search ↗).

source.rightsNote: The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons was published in 1928 by the Ralston University Press, and works first published in the United States before 1931 are in the public domain there — so this sentence, in its 1928 wording, is free to quote. Later revised editions of Hill’s books are separately edited and carry their own modern copyright; the public-domain status attaches to the 1928 text, not to a current paperback.

author.name: Napoleon Hill
author.heading: Who wrote it
author.bio: Born in Pound, Virginia in 1883, Hill worked as a journalist and salesman before turning to success writing. His eight-volume course The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons appeared in 1928, and Think and Grow Rich — the book that made him a household name — followed in 1937. He died in Greenville, South Carolina in 1970. Historians have long questioned the biography he sold alongside the philosophy, including his claim to have worked with Andrew Carnegie.

misattribution.heading: The mix-up worth knowing
misattribution.intro: Nobody is stealing this line from Napoleon Hill — the author credit is right. What goes wrong is the book, and the wording.

items.why: Hill’s most famous book has a chapter headed “Desire: The Starting Point of All Achievement,” and states in the body “The starting point of all achievement is DESIRE.” Those are close cousins, not this sentence — a full text of the book contains no “deeply rooted desire” wording anywhere (full text ↗).

items.who: Modern revised editions of The Law of Success
items.why: A reader checking a current edition may not find the popular wording. The revised “21st-Century Edition” edited by Ann and Bill Hartley compresses Hill’s 1928 sentences into one: “Strong, deeply rooted desire is the starting point and seed of all achievement” (revised-edition scan ↗).

misattribution.truthLine: The sentence is Hill’s own, printed under the sub-heading DESIRE in Lesson Eleven, “Accurate Thought,” of The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons (1928) — nine years before Think and Grow Rich (1928 text ↗).

context.heading: Why this sentence, in this book
lead: The Law of Success was the eight-volume correspondence course Hill built his career on, published in 1928 by the Ralston University Press — the sprawling original that Think and Grow Rich would later boil down into a single paperback (Wikipedia ↗). The line lands in the lesson on “Accurate Thought,” where Hill has just described writing out a “definite chief aim” and reading it daily; DESIRE is what he says has to sit underneath it, or the exercise is empty.

Worth knowing who is talking. Hill sold the course on the claim that Andrew Carnegie commissioned it and opened doors to America’s richest men, but historians doubt much of his self-told biography — the Carnegie collaboration “has remained unsupported by any evidence,” and no records survive of the interviews he claimed, beyond a brief photo opportunity with Edison (Wikipedia ↗). The sentence is authentically his. The empire of research he said stood behind it is another question.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's sourced section attributes "Strong, deeply rooted desire is the starting point of all achievement." to The Law of Success (1928), i.e. The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons.

The 1928 Ralston University Press text of The Law of Success in Sixteen Lessons contains verbatim: "Strong, deeply rooted desire is the starting point of all achievement. Just as the electron is the last unit of matter discernible to the scientist, DESIRE is the seed of all achievement; the starting place, back of which there is nothing..." in Lesson Eleven, "Accurate Thought," under the sub-heading DESIRE; the title page reads "Copyright, 1928, by Napoleon Hill" and "The Ralston University Press, Meriden, Conn."
The Internet Archive item page for the 1928 Law of Success scan exists and resolves.

A full text of Think and Grow Rich contains no occurrence of "deeply rooted desire" or of this sentence; it has the chapter heading "Desire: The Starting Point of All Achievement" and the body line "The starting point of all achievement is DESIRE." twice.

A scan of Law of Success: The 21st-Century Edition, Revised and Updated, edited by Ann Hartley and Bill Hartley, renders the passage as "Strong, deeply rooted desire is the starting point and seed of all achievement."

Napoleon Hill was born 26 October 1883 in Pound, Virginia and died 8 November 1970 in Greenville, South Carolina; The Law of Success was published in 1928 by Ralston University Press as an eight-volume work; Think and Grow Rich was published in 1937; his claimed collaboration with Andrew Carnegie "has remained unsupported by any evidence."
A Quote Investigator site search for "starting point of all achievement" returns no investigation of this Napoleon Hill line (the only result concerns a Longfellow-attributed quotation).
